persona.name: Ravi Krishnan
persona.background: Ravi works long desk hours and commutes daily in city traffic. He has had a long history of cigarette smoking and tends to ignore chronic symptoms until they interfere with work.

diagnoses.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
diagnoses.description: Preventable and treatable pulmonary disease characterized by progressive airflow limitation that is not fully reversible and associated with an abnormal inflammatory response to noxious particles or gases.

diagnoses.name: Chronic bronchitis
diagnoses.description: Defined as chronic productive cough for 3 months in each of two successive years in a patient in whom other causes of chronic cough have been excluded.

diagnoses.name: Emphysema
diagnoses.description: An anatomically defined condition with abnormal permanent enlargement of airspaces distal to terminal bronchioles with destruction of airspace walls, without obvious fibrosis.

diagnoses.name: Bronchial asthma
diagnoses.description: Episodes of wheeze, cough and dyspnea with variable airflow obstruction that is often reversible spontaneously or with treatment, associated with airway hyper-reactivity and bronchial inflammation.

diagnoses.name: Bronchiectasis
diagnoses.description: Chronic condition characterized by severe persistent productive cough with foul-smelling, thick, copious, tenacious, continuously purulent sputum; may have recurrent hemoptysis and coarse crepitations/wheezing.

diagnoses.name: Community-acquired pneumonia
diagnoses.description: Acute respiratory illness with inflammation and exudative solidification of lung parenchyma causing consolidation; clinical constellation includes fever, chills, cough, pleural chest pain, sputum and crackles with an opacity on chest X-ray.

diagnoses.name: Bronchopneumonia
diagnoses.description: Widespread focal/patchy acute suppurative inflammation centered on bronchioles/bronchi with spread to surrounding alveoli; commonly bilateral with lower-lobe predominance.

diagnoses.name: Aspiration pneumonia (chemical pneumonitis)
diagnoses.description: Develops due to aspiration of substances toxic to lower airways; presents with abrupt onset of low-grade fever and dyspnea with cyanosis and diffuse crepitations; CXR shows dependent infiltrates within 2 hours.

diagnoses.name: Interstitial lung disease (diffuse parenchymal lung disease)
diagnoses.description: Typically presents chronically with shortness of breath, dry cough, fatigue, weakness, loss of appetite and weight; exam often shows clubbing, cyanosis and crackles (velcro rales); PFT shows restrictive defect with reduced diffusion capacity.

diagnoses.name: Pulmonary sarcoidosis
diagnoses.description: May show bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with/without diffuse pulmonary infiltrates; may present with breathlessness or cough; ACE may be elevated and Mantoux is often reduced/absent.

initialComplaint: I have a daily cough with a lot of thick, foul-smelling sputum, especially when I get up in the morning, and I get breathless on exertion. Sometimes there are streaks of blood when the cough worsens.
medicalHistory: Long-term cigarette smoking. Reports repeated infective exacerbations with increased sputum volume and fever/malaise precipitated by upper respiratory tract infections. No other past history provided.
symptoms:
Severe persistent (chronic) productive cough that is chronic, daily and persistent, with paroxysms when rising in the morning due to postural drainage of secretions. Sputum is foul-smelling, thick, copious, tenacious and continuously purulent, sometimes bloody. Hemoptysis occurs as streaks of blood commonly with exacerbations and may be recurrent. During infective exacerbations, he reports increased sputum volume with fever and malaise/anorexia. He also reports exertional breathlessness/dyspnea and occasional wheezing/orthopnea with more advanced disease.

z Traction theory: Traction of the bronchi walls secondary to fibrosis/scarring.
z Atelectasis theory: Negative intrapleural pressure resulting in collapse and bronchial dilatation.
z All of the above leads to “Vicious Cycle” Bronchiectasis proposed by Cole which comprises of Initial Insult resulting in

neutrophilic inflammation → Airway destruction → Abnormal mucus clearance → Mucus stasis → Bacterial colonization
resulting in further inflammation.

CHAP
relevantFindings:
General examination may reveal anemia, fever during exacerbations, weight loss/weakness and halitosis; sinusitis may be present. Respiratory examination: auscultation reveals crackles and wheezing; presence of large amounts of secretion produces characteristic bilateral, coarse, leathery crepitations (may be palpable). Investigations: blood may show anemia, raised ESR and leukocytosis indicating suppuration; ABG may show respiratory alkalosis or hypoxemia. Sputum may be continuously purulent and can be examined by Gram stain and Ziehl–Neelsen stain with culture and sensitivity (culture often grows organisms including Pseudomonas). If sputum is allowed to stand, it may form three layers (top mucoid, middle mucopurulent, bottom purulent). Chest radiograph may show tram-track opacities or ring shadows; chest CT is more specific and sensitive for bronchiectasis.
